clue.text: Real tennis, perhaps, legitimate object for ridicule

definitions.meaning: real tennis is an old indoor racket sport, read here as a sport that is genuine and above board
someone it is acceptable to mock or attack

explanation.surface: A sneer at real tennis, the old court game, as a fit target for mockery.
explanation.walkthrough: Real tennis is the original indoor racket game; 'real' is read as 'fair', so it is an honest sport, while the phrase also means a proper target for ridicule.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom names a target that may properly be mocked, and the words also describe an honest sporting contest.

clue.text: Little fellow with paper-round is chilled

parts.note: F is the short form of fellow

indicators.note: turned round, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A small boy with a paper round is cold.
explanation.definitionFit: The French past participle describes a drink served iced.

indicators.note: say signals that the phrase is spoken and heard as a different word

parts.note: doing things by rota means in turn, taking turns

explanation.surface: A question about learning by repetition.
explanation.walkthrough: 'By rota' means one after another, which spoken sounds like the word for confine.
explanation.definitionFit: To detain enemy nationals in wartime is to imprison them.

clue.text: Grey-headed, silver leg variety of geese

indicators.note: only the head, the first letter, of the word is taken

parts.note: Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

indicators.note: a variety of the word, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A breed of geese with a grey head and silvery legs.
explanation.definitionFit: A flock of the birds on the ground has its own collective noun.

indicators.note: money paid out is dispersed, so the letters are scattered and rearranged

explanation.surface: A grand total of money has been paid.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wonderful or astonishing is remarkable.

clue.text: An apartment has nothing in it that is free of debt

indicators.note: the apartment holds the nothing inside it, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a flat is an apartment
nothing is zero, the letter O

explanation.surface: An empty flat belongs to someone who owes no money.
explanation.definitionFit: A business that is solvent, not sinking under liabilities, is said to be keeping its head above water.

clue.text: Dowdy hag, say, taking in seat?

indicators.note: the fish takes the seat into its middle

parts.note: the hag is a fish, the hagfish
the rump is the seat, the backside

explanation.surface: An old crone sitting down looks shabby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hag' looks like a crone, but the 'say' marks it as an example of a fish, the hagfish.
explanation.definitionFit: Unfashionable and drab describes a dull, old-fashioned dresser.

clue.text: Job, say, for speaker at No. 10

parts.note: an orator is a public speaker
the number 10 is written as the letters I and O

explanation.surface: A job for a spokesman at Downing Street.
explanation.walkthrough: No. 10 is Downing Street, the Prime Minister's residence; here it is just 1 and 0, IO. Job is the Bible figure, subject of a choral work by Parry.
explanation.definitionFit: A large choral work on a sacred theme, such as Parry's Job, belongs to this form.

clue.text: Setting for important events in Mayfair and

parts.note: auto- is the prefix meaning self
giro is a system of banking transfers

explanation.surface: An old flying machine that tilts its own wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Self-banking' reads as an aircraft that tilts on its own; giro is the British term for a bank transfer system, as in a giro cheque.
explanation.definitionFit: The rotary-winged machine of the 1920s and 30s was a forerunner of the helicopter.

clue.text: Clergyman who puts value on copper

indicators.note: in an across clue the rate is written after, so it sits on the copper

parts.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
to rate is to put a value on something

explanation.surface: A priest who appraises copper coins.
explanation.definitionFit: An assistant parish priest in the Church of England holds this title.

indicators.note: a setting arranges stones, so the letters of the phrase are rearranged

explanation.surface: A matching jewel set entirely with pearls.
explanation.definitionFit: A counterpart that matches another exactly is its equivalent, a match.

parts.note: reads as springtime in Belgium's capital, but means the shoot that springs up on a Brussels plant, the small green vegetable

explanation.surface: A question about the season in the Belgian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: To spring up is to shoot; the Brussels plant gives the small green vegetable.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both to spring up as a shoot and the small cabbage-like vegetable from Brussels.

indicators.note: subtly altered, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: Cleverly overshadowing a piece of a public vote.
explanation.definitionFit: A direct vote of a whole electorate on one question is a popular ballot.

parts.note: a medicine aimed at one particular disease rather than many

explanation.surface: A drug that does not treat a wide range of ailments.
explanation.definitionFit: In medicine the noun names a remedy targeted at one particular illness.

clue.text: Poisoning from bangers, mainly, but limos can produce it

indicators.note: the letters can produce the answer when rearranged

explanation.surface: Food poisoning usually comes from sausages, though a limousine can cause it too.
explanation.walkthrough: Bangers are British sausages; the illness takes its name from Latin botulus, sausage. 'it' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A serious illness caused by a bacterial toxin in badly preserved food was first linked to sausages.

parts.note: de is French for of
a man engaged to be married is a fiance

explanation.surface: A French bridegroom-to-be faces a challenge.
explanation.definitionFit: Open resistance or a bold dare is a challenge.

parts.note: reads as grammar, the accusative case of a pronoun, but means the person whose case in court is the accusing one

explanation.surface: A grammar lesson about the object form of a pronoun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Accusative case' looks like grammar; here it is the accusing case put by one side in a trial.
explanation.definitionFit: The lawyer who brings charges against the defendant presents the accusing case at trial.

indicators.note: a resort here means a re-sorting of the letters, not a holiday town

explanation.surface: Drawing near the seaside town of St Malo.
explanation.walkthrough: St Malo is a resort in Brittany, but 're-sort' rearranges its letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Nearly, very nearly there, describes something approaching.

definitions.meaning: a line of descent or breed, as in a bloodline
to tax is to stretch or overwork

explanation.surface: A levy on blood.
explanation.definitionFit: A bloodline or breed, and to put pressure on or overwork.

clue.text: Part of meal taken from chosen trees

indicators.note: the letters are taken out of the run of words

explanation.surface: Part of a dinner made from selected trees.
explanation.definitionFit: A course served at a meal, the main dish in the US.

clue.text: German relative changing coins around university

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the university letter
the coins are changed, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A relative from Germany exchanging money near a campus.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' rearranges COINS to COSIN, which goes 'around' U. A cousin-german is a first cousin, so 'German' is part of the definition, not a nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A cousin-german is an old term for a first cousin, a child of an uncle or aunt.

parts.note: a round of ammunition is a bullet
in means popular or fashionable

explanation.surface: A question whether a news programme is well liked.
explanation.walkthrough: Newsround is a BBC children's news programme; split, 'News' defines and 'round' is a bullet.
explanation.definitionFit: A short official announcement or broadcast report gives news.

indicators.note: only the first half of the weekday's name is kept

parts.note: Friday is a day of the week
the close of something is its end

explanation.surface: A Chinese shop shuts early one afternoon a week.
explanation.walkthrough: China means mate in Cockney rhyming slang, from china plate; 'half' cuts FRIDAY to FRI.
explanation.definitionFit: In Cockney rhyming slang china plate rhymes with mate, a pal.

clue.text: Out of date thing is around no longer

indicators.note: the words are no longer in their original form, so their letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Something old-fashioned has stopped being present.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing hopelessly behind the times is likened to an extinct reptile.

parts.note: reads as a branch of a retail bank, but means the raised slope across a main road

explanation.surface: A question about a bank on the main shopping street.
explanation.walkthrough: A road is built higher in the middle so water runs off; that slight banking is the camber.
explanation.definitionFit: The convex curve or tilt of a road surface is a slope, a raised cross-section.

definitions.meaning: as in 'at the ... of', at someone's pressing request
an occasion, as in 'for the first time'

explanation.surface: Someone presses hard for more time.
explanation.definitionFit: An old sense means insistent asking; the everyday sense is an occasion or example.
